chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Hamza ibn Humran, from his father, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, when it is His will to honor a servant who has a sin, He tests him with sickness. If He does not do that for him, He tests him with need (poverty). If He does not do that with him, He makes death difficult for him to compensate for that sin with it.

He (peace be upon him) said: And when it is His will to humble a servant who has a good deed with Him, He grants health to his body. If He does not do that with him, He expands his sustenance for him. If he does not do that with him, He eases death for him to compensate for that good deed with it.
ai.seo_question: What is the wisdom behind illness, poverty, and death in Shia theology?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the concept of *tadhyil* (hastening recompense), where God uses worldly afflictions or blessings to settle a servant's spiritual account before the Hereafter. Specifically, it highlights the paradox that trials like sickness or poverty may be signs of divine honor for a sinner, while ease and health may serve to humble a righteous person, ensuring their good deeds are fully rewarded in this life.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al Hassan Bin Mahboub, from Abdulah Bin Sinan, from Hamza Bin Humran, from his father, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Says: “When it was from His<sup>azwj</sup> Command that He<sup>azwj</sup> Honours a servant and there is a sin for him, He<sup>azwj</sup> would Try him with the sickness. So if He<sup>azwj</sup> does not Do that to him, He<sup>azwj</sup> would Try him with the need. So if He<sup>azwj</sup> does not Do that with him, He<sup>azwj</sup> would Make the death to be more difficult upon him in order to Make it expiation for the sin with that’.

He<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said: ‘And when it was from His<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Command that He<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Humiliates a servant and there is a sin for him, would Grant health to his body. So if He<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> does not Do that with him, He<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> would Expand his sustenance upon him. So if he does not Do that with him, He<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> would Ease the death upon him for the compensation of his good deed’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from al-Hassan ibn Mahbub from ‘Abd Allah ibn Sinan from Hamza ibn Humran from his father from abu Ja’far (a.s.) who has said the following:

“Of the decision of Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, in the affairs of a servant whom He honors and who has a sin, is that Allah causes him to suffer certain illnesses. If He does not do this He causes him to become needy, if He does not do this He causes death to become very difficult for him to compensate from him for the sin. ’

“The Imam said, ‘Also of the decision of Allah, in the case of a person who is insignificant to Him, but he has good deeds before Allah, is that He grants him good health. If He does not do this. He expands the means of living for him and if He does not do this to him also He causes death to become easy for him to match his good deed.’”
